title: The usage of accept() is not recommended, it's better to use accept4().
summary: Without this flag, an opened sensitive file descriptor would remain open across a fork+exec to a lower-privileged SELinux domain. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: Accept4() should include SOCK_CLOEXEC in its type argument to avoid the file descriptor leakage.
summary: Without this flag, an opened sensitive file would remain open across a fork+exec to a lower-privileged SELinux domain. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: The usage of creat() is not recommended, it's better to use open().
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: The usage of dup() is not recommended, it's better to use fcntl(), which can set the close-on-exec flag.

title: Fopen() should include e in their mode string; so re would be valid.
summary: This is equivalent to having set FD_CLOEXEC on that descriptor. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: Memfd_create() should include MFD_CLOEXEC in its type argument to avoid the file descriptor leakage.
summary: Without this flag, an opened sensitive file would remain open across a fork+exec to a lower-privileged SELinux domain. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: A common source of security bugs is code that opens a file without using the O_CLOEXEC flag.
summary: Without that flag, an opened sensitive file would remain open across a fork+exec to a lower-privileged SELinux domain, leaking that sensitive data. Open-like functions including open(), openat(), and open64() should include O_CLOEXEC in their flags argument. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: This check detects usage of pipe().
summary: Using pipe() is not recommended, pipe2() is the suggested replacement. The check also adds the O_CLOEXEC flag that marks the file descriptor to be closed in child processes. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: This check ensures that pipe2() is called with the O_CLOEXEC flag.
summary: The check also adds the O_CLOEXEC flag that marks the file descriptor to be closed in child processes. Without this flag a sensitive file descriptor can be leaked to a child process, potentially into a lower-privileged SELinux domain. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: Socket() should include SOCK_CLOEXEC in its type argument to avoid the file descriptor leakage.
summary: Without this flag, an opened sensitive file would remain open across a fork+exec to a lower-privileged SELinux domain. clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.

title: Diagnoses comparisons that appear to be incorrectly placed in the argument to the TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY macro.
summary: Having such a use is incorrect in the vast majority of cases, and will often silently defeat the purpose of the TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY macro. The check is in the android module of clang-tidy.
